ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Persistent nonunion

A 37-year-old construction worker reports chronic wrist pain and reduced motion months after an untreated scaphoid injury. Imaging shows persistent nonunion with degenerative change around the wrist. Which long-term complication is most consistent with this course?

  1. De Quervain tenosynovitis
  2. Isolated median nerve entrapment
  3. Primary inflammatory polyarthritis
  4. Post-traumatic wrist arthritis
  5. Kienbock disease
Answer and explanation

Post-traumatic wrist arthritis

Unhealed scaphoid injury can disrupt wrist mechanics and lead to degenerative change.

Option explanations

Post-traumatic wrist arthritis: Unhealed scaphoid injury can disrupt wrist mechanics and lead to degenerative change.

Kienbock disease: This concerns avascular necrosis of the lunate, rather than degenerative change secondary to scaphoid nonunion.

De Quervain tenosynovitis: This involves the first dorsal tendon compartment and does not explain the nonunion-associated joint degeneration.

Isolated median nerve entrapment: Nerve compression may cause sensory symptoms but does not explain this structural radiographic pattern.

Primary inflammatory polyarthritis: The localized degenerative findings following an unhealed fracture favor a post-traumatic process.
